rationale: Re-review after fixes. All 4 critical findings resolved: CR-006 (multi-tool-call confirm-shows-one-executes-all) fixed in tool_call_confirmation_mixin.py; CR-009 (cross-assistant resume with no ownership check) fixed in assistant.py resume_tool_call; CR-010 (request override could lower assistant's hard-ceiling policy) fixed by restoring ToolCallPolicy.stricter() clamp in tool_permissions_service.py, with tests updated to assert the hard-ceiling behavior in both directions (test_request_override_raises_above_assistant, test_request_override_cannot_lower_assistant_ceiling, test_conversation_policy_raises_above_assistant, test_conversation_policy_cannot_lower_assistant_ceiling); CR-011 (floor policy string not coerced to enum, crashing stricter()) fixed by coercing to ToolCallPolicy before use. CR-002 (customer-config.yaml teamsBotIntegration flag) confirmed as accidental rebase-conflict damage, not intentional, and reverted back to true separately from this feature's own diff. Remaining 7 findings (CR-001, CR-003, CR-004, CR-005, CR-007, CR-008, CR-012) are explicitly accepted as-is by author/reviewer decision and deferred rather than blocking this MR; none are security-critical bypasses. Full test suite passes (15653 passed, 164 skipped, 0 failed) and make ruff is clean.

finding_status.notes: make run / pyproject.toml uvicorn config accepted as-is per author decision; unrelated to tool-call-confirmation feature scope.
teamsBotIntegration.enabled flip confirmed accidental (rebase conflict resolution damage) and reverted back to true in config/customer/customer-config.yaml.
New-message-clears-pending-confirmation race accepted as-is per author decision; follow-up if it surfaces in practice.
Unbounded recursion on APPROVE_FOR_ME auto-resume accepted as-is per author decision.
Optional[X] vs X|None typing convention in new modules accepted as-is per author decision; style-only, non-blocking.
ask_for_tool_confirmation / resume path fixed in tool_call_confirmation_mixin.py so Allow no longer silently executes unreviewed sibling tool calls from the same batch.
reject_tool_call(None) race leaving stream open accepted as-is per author decision.
Conversation.tool_call_policy column vs stated out-of-scope: accepted as-is per author decision; design-doc reconciliation to follow separately, not a code defect.
resume_tool_call now verifies the conversation's assistant_id matches the URL's assistant_id before resuming, closing the cross-assistant authorization/config-confusion bypass.

Restored ToolCallPolicy.stricter() hard-ceiling clamp in tool_permissions_service.py so a request/conversation override can only raise strictness above the assistant's configured policy, never lower it. Stale tests asserting the old (insecure) override-wins behavior replaced with tests asserting the ceiling in both directions.
Customer floor policy setting now coerced to ToolCallPolicy enum before being passed to stricter(), preventing the AttributeError crash for any tenant configuring min_tool_call_policy.
Non-conforming commit message formats in history accepted as-is per author decision; not re-worded to avoid rewriting already-shared history.
